primitives.name: Pass Location Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: First, we introduce an image processing tool designed specifically for extracting the raw data from the NGS pass charts.
primitives.assumptions: Pass charts are accurately rendered and contain sufficient resolution for pixel-level extraction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Chart rendering distortion or low-resolution images impair extraction accuracy.

layer2.mapping: Maps 2D pixel coordinates from NGS charts to normalized field coordinates for spatial analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of extracted coordinates vs. known ground truth positions.

primitives.name: Completion Percentage Above Expectation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We introduce a Naive Bayes approach for estimating the 2-D completion percentage surfaces of individual teams and quarterbacks, and we provide a one-number summary, completion percentage above expectation (CPAE), for evaluating quarterbacks and team defenses.
primitives.assumptions: Pass outcomes follow independent Bernoulli trials within spatial bins; prior estimates are informative but not overly restrictive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small sample sizes in sparse field regions cause unstable estimates.

layer2.mapping: Maps observed pass completions to expected completion rates under baseline models, producing scalar performance metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between estimated and actual NFL CPAE values.

primitives.name: Spatial Completion Modeling
primitives.verbatim_quote: We use a generalized additive model for completion percentages by field location.
primitives.assumptions: Completion rates vary smoothly across space and can be approximated by basis functions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-stationarity in play dynamics or extreme outliers disrupt smoothness assumptions.

layer2.mapping: Produces 2D surfaces of expected completion probability conditioned on spatial location.
layer2.telemetry: Goodness-of-fit measures against empirical pass outcome distributions.
